Hi Andreia, it's David. Congratulations on the invitation to chair the nursing session. A few tips from someone who has chaired many panels. First, start with the housekeeping, and keep it short: exits, breaks and the time for questions. Second, protect the time slots. If a panelist overruns, do not wait until the end. Interrupt politely and give them thirty seconds to finish. Third, watch the quiet people. If one panelist has not said anything, bring them in with a direct question. And if the discussion gets sidetracked, use a simple phrase like coming back to our main question. Finally, finish on time, thank everybody, and ask for a round of applause. People always remember a session that ends on time.

Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to this session on the nurse's role in robotic surgery. My name is Andreia Heins, and I am a nurse at Einstein Hospital in Sao Paulo. I will be your moderator today. Before we start, a little housekeeping. The exits are at the back of the room, and the coffee break is at three thirty.
